title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate
description: Validates ability to design and implement secure and robust solutions using AWS technologies and Well-Architected Framework pillars.

questions.statement: A company hosts a static website on Amazon S3 and distributes the content globally via Amazon CloudFront. The security team requires users to access files exclusively through the CloudFront URL and never directly through the S3 bucket endpoint. What is the recommended configuration?

options.text: Configure Origin Access Control (OAC) on the CloudFront distribution and update the S3 bucket policy to allow access only from that distribution.
options.explanation: Correct: OAC is the current secure AWS recommendation to restrict S3 bucket access solely to designated CloudFront distributions.

options.text: Make the S3 bucket public and block direct traffic using Security Group rules.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 buckets do not use Security Groups.

options.text: Use Pre-signed URLs for all public page read requests.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Pre-signed URLs are intended for restricted temporary access, not public static websites.

options.text: Create an S3 VPC Endpoint and route CloudFront distribution into a private subnet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudFront is a global edge service and does not run inside private VPC subnets.

questions.generalExplanation: Origin Access Control (OAC) supersedes legacy OAI and enables Amazon CloudFront to authenticate with S3 buckets via SigV4, completely restricting direct public access to S3.

questions.statement: An order processing application experiences unpredictable traffic spikes. Each order takes an average of 2 minutes to process. Solutions architects need to decouple the web tier from the backend processing tier to ensure no orders are dropped during spikes and the backend scales automatically based on demand. Which TWO options meet these requirements? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use an Amazon SQS queue between the web tier and the order processing tier.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon SQS decouples components and durably buffers messages until consumers can process them.

options.text: Configure a Target Tracking Scaling Policy on the worker Auto Scaling group based on the customized SQS metric ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible.
options.explanation: Correct: Scaling based on queue depth backlog per instance ensures capacity scales proportionally to pending message volume.

options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions directly to the processing instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Sticky sessions do not decouple tiers and may overload specific worker nodes.

options.text: Configure Amazon SNS topics with synchronous HTTP delivery to backend servers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SNS HTTP delivery does not provide a durable buffering queue if workers are temporarily overwhelmed.

options.text: Replace the backend with Spot EC2 instances in a fixed-size Auto Scaling group without an intermediate queue.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Spot instances can be interrupted and fixed size cannot handle unpredictable traffic bursts without a buffer.

questions.generalExplanation: The standard AWS architectural pattern for resilient asynchronous decoupling is using Amazon SQS queues with EC2 Auto Scaling groups scaled according to queue backlog depth per instance.

questions.statement: A news web application with high read volume and low write volume is experiencing database performance degradation due to repetitive SQL queries on an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Which solution will improve read performance most cost-effectively and quickly?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of Amazon RDS and implement a Lazy Loading (Cache-Aside) caching strategy.
options.explanation: Correct: In-memory ElastiCache dramatically reduces read latency to sub-milliseconds and offloads repetitive read queries from the relational database.

options.text: Migrate the RDS database to larger instance types with io2 Block Express EBS volumes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Vertical scaling with io2 is far more expensive and does not solve repetitive in-memory caching efficiency.

options.text: Enable Multi-AZ on RDS and direct SELECT queries to the secondary standby instance.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Traditional RDS Multi-AZ standby instances are passive for failover and do not accept read traffic (unlike Aurora or dedicated Read Replicas).

options.text: Enable AWS Auto Scaling directly on the RDS MySQL primary node.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard RDS MySQL single instances do not support instantaneous on-demand compute node auto-scaling for reads like ElastiCache.

questions.generalExplanation: An in-memory caching layer with Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) using the Cache-Aside pattern is the recommended AWS best practice for read-heavy relational database workloads.

questions.statement: A healthcare provider generates medical scan images that need to be accessed frequently for the first 30 days. After 30 days, images are rarely accessed but must be retained for 5 years due to legal compliance, with a retrieval time of up to 5 hours acceptable. What is the most cost-effective Amazon S3 lifecycle strategy?

options.text: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days, and expire/delete them after 5 years.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Standard covers initial active access, while S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval provides low-cost long-term storage for 3-5 hour retrieval requirements.

options.text: Store all files in S3 Glacier Deep Archive from the start with expedited retrieval.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Glacier Deep Archive does not support initial frequent access and does not offer expedited retrieval.

options.text: Transition objects to S3 One Zone-IA after 30 days and retain for 5 years.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 One Zone-IA has higher storage costs than Glacier and lower resilience (single AZ), which is not suitable for critical medical data.

options.text: Keep objects in S3 Standard and manually apply gzip compression after 30 days.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Keeping files in S3 Standard for 5 years incurs excessive costs and manual compression creates high operational overhead.

questions.generalExplanation: Automated transition via S3 Lifecycle to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval minimizes long-term storage costs while maintaining compliant availability within acceptable retrieval timeframes.
